summary: Documents extensions to LDP and RSVP that the Optical Internetworking Forum defined for optical user network interface signaling. They consist of new data objects and error codes, and this informational memo records them and their assigned values.

eli5.summary: The Optical Internetworking Forum added new message parts for optical connections. This note writes down those parts so their numbers are on record.

questions: optical uni signaling ldp rsvp extensions
subtitle: Protocol extensions for optical network interface signaling.

tldr.problem: Optical networks need to signal connection setup and management across user network interfaces, but the standard LDP and RSVP protocols did not have all the data structures and capabilities needed for optical UNI signaling.
tldr.mechanism: The Optical Internetworking Forum defined extensions to both LDP (seven new TLVs for source/destination addresses, labels, and service parameters) and RSVP (a Generalized_UNI object and new error codes) to support optical UNI signaling.
tldr.outcome: This document allocates and documents the IANA code points for these extensions, enabling interoperable optical UNI implementations. It was updated by RFC 3468.

today: RFC 3476 is an Informational document published in March 2003. It was updated by RFC 3468, which consolidates and refines IANA assignments for multiple GMPLS protocols including LDP and RSVP extensions.

sections.title: Introduction and Scope
sections.content:
The Optical Interworking Forum (OIF) has defined the UNI (User Network Interface) specification to enable optical networks to dynamically establish and manage connections. The UNI specification reuses IETF protocols including LDP (Label Distribution Protocol) and RSVP (Resource ReSerVation Protocol), maximizing compatibility with existing infrastructure.

However, optical UNI signaling requires capabilities beyond the base LDP and RSVP specifications. This document describes the extensions that OIF defined and requests IANA allocation of code points for them, ensuring globally unique identifiers across all implementations.
sections.eli5: Optical networks use standard signaling systems (LDP and RSVP), but they need extra information fields for things like selecting output ports and quality levels. This document reserves identification numbers for all those new fields.

sections.title: LDP Extensions for Optical UNI
sections.content:
LDP is extended with seven new Type-Length-Value (TLV) structures specific to optical UNI signaling:

Source and Destination ID TLVs: Three TLVs each encode source and destination identifiers in IPv4 (codes 0x0960, 0x0963), IPv6 (codes 0x0961, 0x0964), or NSAP (codes 0x0962, 0x0965) formats, allowing flexible addressing across different network address types.

Egress Label TLV (code 0x0966): Specifies the label or port that optical traffic should use when leaving the network.

Local Connection ID TLV (code 0x0967): Identifies a connection within a local domain, enabling correlation between related requests.

Diversity TLV (code 0x0968): Indicates that the requested connection should take a different path from an existing connection (for redundancy).

Contract ID TLV (code 0x0969): References a service contract or agreement that governs the connection parameters.

UNI Service Level TLV (code 0x0970): Specifies the quality of service or service level for the connection.
sections.eli5: LDP is extended with seven new kinds of information. These say where the data comes from and goes to, which output port to use, whether it needs to avoid other paths, what contract applies, and what service quality is needed.

sections.title: RSVP Extensions for Optical UNI
sections.content:
RSVP is extended with two new structures for optical UNI signaling:

Generalized_UNI Object (Class 229, C-Type 1): A container object that holds variable-length sub-objects. The sub-objects include Source Transport Network Assigned (TNA) Address (Type 1, with IPv4, IPv6, and NSAP subtypes), Destination TNA Address (Type 2, with subtypes), Diversity (Type 3), Egress Label (Type 4), and Service Level (Type 5). This object carries UNI-specific parameters in RSVP messages.

UNI_IPv4_Session Object (Class 1, C-Type 11): An extension to the RSVP Session object that includes an IPv4 address, tunnel ID, and extended IPv4 address fields specific to optical UNI sessions. The C-Type value 11 distinguishes UNI-related sessions from other RSVP sessions.

Error Codes: Five new UNI-specific error sub-codes are defined under two RSVP error classes: Routing Problem (error code 24) includes Diversity not available (sub-code 100), Service level not available (101), and Invalid/Unknown connection ID (102); Policy Control Failure (error code 2) includes Unauthorized sender (100) and Unauthorized receiver (101).
sections.eli5: RSVP is extended with a container object that carries UNI-specific information, a special session type for optical connections, and error codes that describe optical-specific problems like 'the network is too busy to deliver the quality you requested' or 'you are not authorized to use that connection'.

sections.title: IANA Code Point Allocations
sections.content:
The document requests IANA to allocate the following code points in the LDP and RSVP name spaces:

LDP TLV Types: 0x0960 through 0x0970 for the seven new TLVs described above. UNI-specific status codes are allocated from the private use space (0x3Fxxxxxx) and do not require IANA administration.

RSVP Object Classes and Sub-codes: The Generalized_UNI object (Class 229, C-Type 1) and its sub-objects (Types 1-5 with various sub-types); the UNI_IPv4_Session object (Class 1, C-Type 11); and the five new error sub-codes (codes 24 sub-codes 100-102, and code 2 sub-codes 100-101) as described in Section 3.3.
sections.eli5: The document formally reserves these ID numbers so that when two optical network systems talk to each other, they both understand 0x0960 means 'Source ID in IPv4 format' and Class 229 means 'This is a Generalized_UNI object'. Without these reservations, vendors might accidentally use the same numbers for different things.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Security aspects of the UNI extensions are described in the OIF UNI specification and inherit the security properties of LDP (RFC 3036), RSVP (RFC 2205), and RSVP-TE (RFC 3209). The extensions themselves do not introduce new security mechanisms but rely on the underlying protocol security.

The RSVP error code for "Unauthorized sender" and "Unauthorized receiver" allows UNI implementations to enforce access control policies at network boundaries. Additional security considerations pertaining to UNI signaling are addressed in the OIF UNI specification itself.
sections.eli5: The extensions follow the same security rules as the base LDP and RSVP protocols. They add error codes so the network can reject unauthorized users, but they do not add new encryption or authentication features.
